## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Stock OpenCode V2 binaries can now be installed with integrity checks against both a repository-recorded digest and the release’s `SHA256SUMS`. The pin currently records V2.2.0; the workspace image verifies its musl asset too, while the default remains on the existing V1 harness path. [#1973](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1973)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Workflows that still pass the five `enable-omo`, `enable-omo-slim`, `omo-version`, `omo-providers` or `omo-slim-preset` inputs will now get GitHub’s “Unexpected input” annotation and continue using the default configuration. The Action no longer installs oMo or oMo Slim, their agents, or provider routing; use the `build` agent, bundled Systematic plugin, and `agent`, `model`, `auth-json` and `opencode-config` inputs instead. Provider configuration must now be set through `auth-json` and `opencode-config`. [#1968](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1968)

The removal also eliminates the oMo-specific Bun installation path and plugin/configuration guards. The tools cache now uses a v2 key, so each runner will incur one cold cache miss after upgrading; the default generated config remains unchanged. [#1968](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1968)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

The Action and workspace image now default to the patched OpenCode 1.19.4 harness. Its 15 local carries were retained and verified against the upstream release, and the harness build, SDK, and Bun versions are aligned; the harness also accounts for upstream changes to update checks and session sharing. [#1959](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1959) [#1962](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1962)

Runs now wait for OpenCode’s `server.connected` event before sending a prompt, so permissions, early output, idle state, and errors emitted immediately after the prompt are not lost. If the event stream never connects, the attempt fails before sending the prompt and can retry on a fresh stream; the same connection barrier is used by both the gateway and Action. [#1956](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1956)

An early abort on a cold or still-preparing session could previously look stopped before the prompt had actually started, releasing the session for another run. The gateway now requires a terminal reply to the latest user turn as positive stop evidence, re-aborts while a root remains live, and quarantines sessions when that evidence is missing; runs that never sent a prompt keep the fast path. [#1965](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1965)

CI now selects Bun from the root `packageManager` field and checks that the installed version matches it, replacing duplicated workflow version literals that had left jobs on an older Bun during harness verification. [#1963](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1963)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Operators can now see why an active gateway run is still draining, rather than seeing only a generic running state. The live status reports one of four bounded reasons—agent work, a pending reply, background-task completion, or completion confirmation—and refreshes only when the reason changes; approval and question prompts take precedence. The reason is in-memory status only, is omitted from run summaries, and is cleared when the event loop exits. [#1954](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1954)

Gateway run records are now more likely to reach an accurate terminal state when storage writes fail. Terminal writes retry with bounded attempts and re-check record ownership before writing, while failure replies and operator updates proceed without waiting for the write; a periodic sweep reconciles stale executing or acknowledged records during gateway uptime, leaving queued work untouched. [#1950](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1950)
